result.summary: Re-gate scoped to commit 244c9e1, the rework closing my prior FAIL (handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-02b-reviewer.json, BLOCKER: zero-active-chapters silently stranded a user after noActiveChapters). FIX VERIFIED BY READING: both makeStartHandler and makeConsentCallbackHandler in apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts now seed a local `hasChapter = flowUser.chapterId !== null`, and set it to `true` when assignChapterOrPrompt returns "continue" (covering both the 1-chapter-silently-assigned case and the 0-active-chapters case where chapterId legitimately stays null forever), before calling advanceOnboarding -- replacing the old re-derivation `(finalUser?.chapterId ?? flowUser.chapterId) !== null`, which was exactly the bug. This genuinely mirrors handlers/profile.ts's reachReadyOrPrompt helper (read lines 176-198): that helper already treats a "continue" chapterOutcome as chapter-resolved without re-checking chapterId. Same treatment, same reasoning, now applied symmetrically at all call sites. 2. LIVE-VERIFIED MYSELF, independently of BACKEND-DEV's own test and independently of BACKEND-DEV's own prior live-verification script (wrote and ran my own throwaway apps/bot/src/handlers/__reviewer_verify.test.ts, deleted after use -- git status confirmed clean). Stood up apps/bot/docker-compose.yml's scratch Postgres myself (docker compose up -d, port 55432), ran `DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx drizzle-kit migrate` (applied cleanly), then dispatched real bot.handleUpdate() updates through a real grammY Bot wired to the actual exported handlers, network replaced by a capturing api.config.use transformer (no token, no real Telegram call): - Fresh user, zero active chapters, /start then consent:agree: captured sequence [answerCallbackQuery, sendMessage('Отделения пока недоступны.' / start.noActiveChapters), sendMessage('Как вас зовут (имя)?' / profile.promptFirstName)]. No dead end. - Returning user (consent already recorded via recordConsent, no chapter), zero active chapters, direct /start: captured sequence [sendMessage(start.noActiveChapters), sendMessage(profile.promptFirstName)]. No dead end. finalUser.chapterId confirmed still null afterward (correct -- zero chapters exist, nothing to assign). Both match BACKEND-DEV's own reported evidence exactly, now independently reproduced rather than trusted. 3. makeChapterCallbackHandler CONFIRMED UNCHANGED AND CORRECTLY SO: read it in full (start.ts lines 462-512). It only ever fires after a real chapter was just assigned via assignChapter in the same handler body, and calls advanceOnboarding with a literal `true` for hasChapter, never re-derived from a stale read -- there was never a bug here, and BACKEND-DEV's claim that it needed no change is correct. 4. NEW TEST VERIFIED: read apps/bot/src/handlers/start.test.ts in full. Both cases dispatch real bot.handleUpdate() against the real (non-mocked) handlers and a real migrated Postgres, TRUNCATE all three relevant tables in beforeEach (chapters included, so no leftover chapter row can accidentally satisfy the zero-active-chapters premise), and assert the exact captured method+text sequence through to profile.promptFirstName -- the precise assertion that fails against the pre-fix code (BACKEND-DEV reports re-running against a pre-fix stash and observing the second sendMessage never arrives; I did not re-stash and re-confirm this specific claim myself since I independently reproduced the identical pass/fail-shape via my own from-scratch script instead, which is equivalent evidence). This suite would have caught the original regression. 5. These numbers match BACKEND-DEV's own reported 142+2/144 exactly, using BACKEND-DEV's own clarified canonical invocation (no --root override) -- confirms BACKEND-DEV's explanation for the earlier 284-count discrepancy (a `--root apps/bot` invocation double-counting src/+dist/ copies) rather than taking that explanation on trust. 6. issues.description: .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml's Test/build job runs `npm test`/`npm run build` with no Postgres service, so apps/bot/src/handlers/start.test.ts's two DB-backed cases (and any future DB-backed test) self-skip in CI today via ctx.skip() -- they only ever execute locally against a developer's own scratch Postgres. Confirmed by reading .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml myself: no postgres service block exists in the job that runs the Test step. Recommend adding a postgres:16-alpine service (matching apps/bot/docker-compose.yml's bot/bot/bot credentials) to that job, plus a migrate step before `npm test`, so this coverage actually gates CI rather than only a developer's local run. First flagged by BACKEND-DEV in handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-02-backend-dev-rework1.json; forwarding per ISSUE_QUEUE.md's protocol (discovering/confirming agent reports to ORCH; ORCH allocates the next id, ISS-0013, and writes the file) rather than filing it myself.

Carried forward unchanged from handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-02b-reviewer.json (not addressed by this rework, not in its scope): decisions/0004-telegram-framework-grammy.md's consequence text has no stated exception for a thin decide-and-send composition function, yet the codebase now has two (handlers/start.ts's assignChapterOrPrompt, domain/onboarding.ts's advanceOnboarding). Recommend a decisions/0004 addendum clarifying that a pure-decision-plus-thin-dispatch split satisfies the framework-free intent.

Carried forward unchanged from handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-02b-reviewer.json (not addressed by this rework, not in its scope): docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md §3.2 still documents advanceOnboarding's return type as Promise<"prompted" | "ready"> (2 values); the implementation correctly has 3 (adding "chapter-needed", required by the same section's own step 4 prose). Recommend a design-doc correction note, same convention as REQ-014.md/REQ-016.md's own prior correction-note precedent.
